_note: Read-only snapshot of BAM GTA as production actually holds it: the clients row PLUS every automation and every step. It is the ONE source of truth for 'what GTA looks like today' - scripts/render-messages.mjs renders from it, api/_gta-message-lock.test.mjs builds its client fixture from it, and api/_gta-step-lock.test.mjs locks the rendered step bodies from it, so a production change cannot be true for one and stale for another. Only fields that exist on the row belong here: an absent field must stay absent, because clientVars() treats absent as 'this academy has no such fact'. THREE EXCEPTIONS, all with the same expiry: `business_email` (migration 20260729T210000) plus `tagline` and `instagram_url` (migration 20260729T230000). None of the three is applied to production yet, so a genuine re-capture today would not carry them. All three hold BECAUSE they are the same rule, not despite it: each value here is the EXACT string that was hardcoded in email-shells.js LOCATIONS until its migration was written, and each migration seeds that same string into GTA's row. So they are a move from code to data, not new facts, and the goldens in api/__goldens__/bam-gta and api/__goldens__/bam-gta-steps stay byte-identical across the move - which is the whole claim those locks exist to make. Leaving them out would make the locks record the DEGRADED pre-migration render instead of production's: no unsubscribe address at all for business_email, and a footer with no tagline sentence and no Instagram link for the other two. api/_gta-message-lock.test.mjs asserts business_email is present AND reaching a parent, and api/_tagline-instagram.test.mjs does the same for the other two, so a re-capture that drops any of them fails loudly instead of quietly locking a worse email. Remove this paragraph once both migrations are applied and a genuine re-capture carries all three columns. FOURTH EXCEPTION, AND IT IS A DIFFERENT SHAPE, SO READ IT SEPARATELY: `public_name` and `address` below are AHEAD of production too, but not because a column is missing - both columns exist and are populated in production right now. It is the VALUES that are pending, from migration 20260729T235000: production still holds public_name 'By Any Means Basketball' and address '2205 Rosemount Cres' (verified by read-only select, 2026-07-29). That migration is the DATA half of deleting the LOCATIONS map from api/email-shells.js: the map pinned GTA's wordmark word, its parent-facing full name, its location tag and its city, and all four of those derive from these two fields. So unlike the three above, this pair does NOT keep the goldens byte-identical - it is what MAKES them change, on purpose and with Zoran's approval: the gold wordmark goes GTA -> TORONTO, the tag goes 'OAKVILLE - GTA' -> 'OAKVILLE', and the full name 'By Any Means Toronto' now comes from the row instead of the pin. Carrying the new values here is what makes the re-taken goldens lock the email GTA will actually send once the migration is applied, instead of locking a half-migrated render that will never exist in production (row-derived identity from the OLD public_name, i.e. a wordmark reading BASKETBALL). If you revert this pair without reverting email-shells.js, the goldens go red and they are right to. Remove this paragraph once 20260729T235000 is applied and a genuine re-capture carries both values. FIFTH entry, and unlike the others this one CLOSES a gap rather than opening one: `facts.location_testimonials` carries BAM GTA's five real testimonials as the store holds them in production (2 starred), in the resolver's own order. It is here because nurture-3 and onboarding-testimonials now render their quotes from the store, so a snapshot with no testimonials makes those two emails lock as HAVING NO QUOTES - which production would never produce, and which would hide the store wiring breaking. These are real families' words: copy them, never edit them, and never invent one. SIXTH entry, same shape as the fourth: the three step values below are AHEAD of production, from migration 20260730T120000. onboarding step 1 body, onboarding step 2 SUBJECT and summer_special step 0 body used to hand-type "By Any Means Basketball" and now carry {{location.name}}, so the academy name in them resolves from public_name like everything else. Production still holds the typed strings until that migration is applied. Carrying the tokenized values here is what makes the re-taken api/__goldens__/bam-gta-steps goldens lock the messages GTA will actually send, rather than a half-migrated state where the shell says Toronto and the copy inside says Basketball. Remove this paragraph once 20260730T120000 is applied and a genuine re-capture carries the tokens. SEVENTH entry, and it is the FOURTH shape again (ahead of production, column missing): `facts.location_entry_note` is BAM GTA's Linbrook venue entry note, from migration 20260730T160000. locations.entry_note does not exist in production yet; that migration adds it and seeds this exact string onto the Linbrook row (1079 Linbrook Rd), which is the venue GTA's training offer points its primary location at and therefore the venue every GTA free trial is booked into (verified by read-only select 2026-07-30: all 43 open GTA opportunities carry the Training offer). Like the first three exceptions this is a move from code to data, not a new fact: the same sentence was hardcoded in api/agent/confirm-automations.js and sent by EVERY academy on a shared automation step, describing GTA's door to parents who had never been to Oakville. UNLIKE those three it does not keep a golden byte-identical, because the code no longer sends it to anyone else. api/_confirm-email-lock.test.mjs renders the morning-of check-in through the real offer -> venue chain off this value and off facts.location_venue, so the same-day golden locks the message a GTA parent will actually receive once the migration lands. Leaving it out would lock GTA as having NO entry note, which is a state production will not hold for more than a day. Remove this paragraph once 20260730T160000 is applied and a genuine re-capture carries the column.

location_testimonials.quote:
We had a great experience with By Any Means Basketball. My kid enjoyed every training session and looked forward to coming each week.
The training is engaging and well structured. The coaches do an excellent job of keeping the kids involved by incorporating games and challenges into the sessions. What stood out to us was that the trainers actively participate in the games with the kids, creating a fun and energetic environment while still teaching important basketball skills.
The coaches are young, approachable, and genuinely listen to the kids. They also take time at the end of each session to have meaningful conversations with the group, which helps build confidence and teamwork.
Since joining, my kid has improved his layups and gained confidence attacking the basket from the wing, getting open, receiving the ball, and finishing plays. It was great to see both his skills and confidence grow.
A special shoutout to Adrian—my kid always enjoyed training with him and thought he was a cool coach. Thank you to the group for creating such a positive learning environment for young players!
location_testimonials.author: Kristina Carrera

location_testimonials.quote:
BAM has been an exceptional experience for our son. He's not naturally the most athletic kid, but he's incredibly creative, talkative, and full of ideas—and what really impressed us is how well the coaches understood that and used his personality to keep him engaged and motivated rather than trying to fit him into a one-size-fits-all program.

This is one activity he genuinely looks forward to every single week. Every time I pick him up, he is absolutely buzzing with energy & happiness. We joke about what they must be putting in the air because he comes out so energized—but honestly, it's just a reflection of how amazing the team is.

The coaches are young, energetic, relatable, and really know how to connect with this generation of kids. They create an environment that's motivating, positive, and fun while still delivering exceptional training. For us, that combination has made all the difference. Highly recommend BAM to any parent looking for a basketball program that truly knows how to bring out the best in kids.
location_testimonials.author: Sabeen S

location_testimonials.quote: Very valuable session for players who wanna develop the right mindset and games, would definitely recommend by any means for basketball training.
